entries.core_move: Compute the time-domain output of a continuous-time LTI system by forming $Y(s)=X(s)H(s)$, simplifying the Laplace-domain product, and applying the inverse Laplace transform.

entries.lesson_title: Finding Step Response from a Transfer Function
entries.core_move: Compute an LTI system's unit-step response by using $X(s)=1/s$, forming $Y(s)=H(s)/s$, and applying inverse Laplace methods to recover the time-domain output.

entries.lesson_title: Finding Impulse Response from a Transfer Function
entries.core_move: Compute the causal impulse response $h(t)$ from a rational transfer function $H(s)$ by expanding $H(s)$ into inverse-Laplace-ready terms and transforming back to the time domain.
Select the transfer-function or frequency-response method that matches the LTI-system input and use $H(s)$ or $H(j\omega)$ to compute the corresponding output behavior.
Evaluate $H(s)$ on the imaginary axis by setting $s=j\omega$, where valid, to obtain $H(j\omega)$ and interpret its magnitude and phase as the LTI system's sinusoidal steady-state response.
Classify an LTI system's stability, decay or growth, and oscillatory behavior from the left-half-plane, right-half-plane, or imaginary-axis locations of the poles of its transfer function $H(s)$.
